facts.fact: ITWeb Africa reports that Malawi's Ministry of ICT proposed a Government Data Sharing Regulation for the National Data Exchange Platform (Boma Lathu), which it describes as currently under implementation.

The Times reports that in 2025 the Department of e-Government failed to operationalise the Enterprise Service Bus meant to let ministries communicate, leaving services in silos, and that it faces pressure in 2026 to onboard all major ministries onto it.

note: The interoperability layer is within one ministry's health records system (a sector system, class other); no national exchange platform is described.
The Enterprise Service Bus is named only as one of five core DMAP priority areas, with no statement of its build state; the 25 e-services onboarding is to the citizen portal (class other).

systems.platform: digital services platform / single government services portal

note: Bomalathu is described as a single portal for e-services (25 being onboarded; used by MRA and NRB), not as a platform carrying data between public bodies' systems, so no exchange fact.

facts.fact: An ICT expert (former ICTAM president) said in January 2026 that the Department of e-Government would be under pressure in 2026 to onboard all major ministries, departments and agencies onto the Enterprise Service Bus for interoperability of government systems, with no count of connected bodies.
